source: Discriminator DESIGNED BY a Grok lane (repr-physical) with its kill threshold stated BEFORE the measurement, then executed by the supervisor. The lane did not get to move the bar after seeing the number.
claim_under_test: Fusing the MoE block can move tok/s.
pre_stated_kill: isolated 26-layer routed+shared MoE wall < 2.5 ms would mean the fixed cost lives in MLA / lm_head / graph and MoE fusion cannot help.
VERDICT: SURVIVES. 4.319 ms against a 2.5 ms kill threshold. MoE fusion is worth building.
WHAT_IT_LOCATES: The MoE WRAPPER -- router, shared expert, score-weighted combine -- costs 1.909 ms, 21.7% of the step, and is pure orchestration rather than expert arithmetic. Fusing it is worth up to 1.28x on decode.
INDEPENDENT_CROSS_VALIDATION: Two different methods now agree. Removal-based ablation put attention at 3.600 ms and the MoE block at 4.018; direct isolation gives 3.488 and 4.319 -- within 3-7%. The ablation's caveat (removing a stage also removes downstream work) and the isolation's caveat (no residual/norm context) are opposite biases, so agreement between them is stronger evidence than either alone.
STILL_TRUE: Attention at 3.488 ms isolated remains the single largest stage, larger than the entire MoE wrapper. The 1.69x attention ceiling stands above the ~1.28x MoE-fusion ceiling.
NOTE_ON_MY_OWN_INSTRUMENT: The lane correctly identified that the quality evaluator's weight -> dense bf16 -> forward path CANNOT measure this: it materialises dense tiles and hides the packed-gather stage entirely. TPS work must not go through the evaluator, which is why no binary/sparse/residual arm in this campaign has a TPS number and why none should be inferred.
